extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of political philosophy, law, and theology; readers of Hobbes' Leviathan
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of Hobbes' normative claims about the relations between civil sovereignty and religion (who may teach, interpret Scripture, and punish religious dissent), plus the theological account of Christ's offices and the timing/nature of his kingship.

rubrics_metrics.name: One chief Governor for State and Religion
rubrics_metrics.description: Governour both of the State, and of the Religion, forbiddeth to be taught: And that Governor must be one; or else there must needs follow Faction, and Civil war in the Common-wealth, between the Church and State...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there is not one chief governor, competing authorities will produce faction and civil war. The civil sovereign must therefore be the single authority that regulates both public religion and state to avoid contradictory doctrines and conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil sovereign as chief pastor/interpreter
rubrics_metrics.description: The Doctors of the Church, are called Pastors; so also are Civill Soveraignes: But if Pastors be not subordinate one to another... Who that one chief Pastor is, according to the law of Nature, hath been already shewn; namely, that it is the Civill Soveraign;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sovereign occupies the role of chief pastor: ecclesiastical ministers are subordinate, and the sovereign is identified as the proper 'chief Pastor' with authority over doctrines taught publicly in the commonwealth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to obey sovereign in external religious practice
rubrics_metrics.description: they to whom God hath not spoken immediately, are to receive the positive commandements of God, from their Soveraign... in every Common-wealth, they who have no supernaturall Revelation to the contrary, ought to obey the laws of their own Soveraign, in the externall acts and profession of Religion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obedience is required for outward acts and public profession of religion; inward thought and belief remain beyond the sovereign's lawful reach because only God knows the heart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punishment of private revelations opposing sovereign religion
rubrics_metrics.description: it was not unlawfull for Abraham, when any of his Subjects should pretend Private Vision, or Spirit, or other Revelation from God, for the countenancing of any doctrine which Abraham should forbid, or when they followed, or adhered to any such pretender, to punish them; and consequently that it is lawfull now for the Soveraign to punish any man that shall oppose his Private Spirit against the Laws
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private claims of revelation that contravene the sovereign's established religion may be treated as offenses subject to punishment because they threaten public unity and the sovereign's authority in religious matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sovereign monopoly on interpretation of Scripture
rubrics_metrics.description: as none but Abraham in his family, so none but the Soveraign in a Christian Common-wealth, can take notice what is, or what is not the Word of God.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the person who represents God's person on earth (the sovereign) may properly interpret divine speech for the commonwealth; individuals are not to 'pry into' or judge whether the sovereign governs as God commands—interpretive bounds are set by the sovereign's laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sovereign authority grounded on consent and promise
rubrics_metrics.description: His authority therefore, as the authority of all other Princes, must be grounded on the Consent of the People, and their Promise to obey him. And so it was: for 'the people'... 'speak thou with us, and we will hear, but let not God speak with us lest we die.' Here was their promise of obedience
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even prophetic or sacerdotal rulers (e.g., Moses) derive effective authority from the people's consent and promise to obey; divine mediation alone does not automatically impose obligation without the people's assent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founder's temporary sovereign authority during establishment
rubrics_metrics.description: whosoever ordereth, and establisheth the Policy, as first founder of a Common-wealth (be it Monarchy, Aristocracy, or Democracy) must needs have Soveraign Power over the people all the while he is doing of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The original founder or lawgiver possesses sovereign power while establishing the polity (example: Moses), because the people promise obedience to the founder's commands during formation of institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prophets and spirits subordinate to the sovereign's spirit
rubrics_metrics.description: no Prophet in the time of Moses, nor pretender to the Spirit of God, but such as Moses had approved, and Authorized... God came down in a cloud, and took of the Spirit that was upon Moses, and gave it to the Seventy Elders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prophecy and prophetic activity are legitimate only insofar as they are authorized by and subordinate to the sovereign's spirit/authority; independent prophetic claims that oppose the sovereign's doctrine are illegitimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sacerdotal commonwealth: High Priest's combined civil and ecclesiastical authority
rubrics_metrics.description: the Civill and Ecclesiasticall Power were both joined together in one and the same person, the High Priest; and ought to bee so, in whosoever governeth by Divine Right; that is, by Authority immediate from God.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under a sacerdotal covenant (as with Aaron's line) the high priest holds supreme authority over both religious worship and civil matters; civil judgments and rites are kept by priests who thereby function as sovereigns under divine right.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monarchy confers sovereignty including supremacy in religion
rubrics_metrics.description: they... 'make us a King to judge us, like all the Nations'... their King shall be their Judge, and goe before them, and fight their battells; that is, he shall have the whole authority, both in Peace and War. In which is contained also the ordering of Religion;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a people elect a king, they transfer both civil and religious supremacy to that monarch; the king's authority over religious matters follows from the people's rejection of priestly rule and their choice to be governed as other nations are.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between rightful authority and actual practice
rubrics_metrics.description: though the power both of State and Religion were in the Kings; yet none of them were uncontrolled in the use of it... So that from the practise of those times, there can no argument be drawn, that the right of Supremacy in Religion was not in the Kings, unlesse we place it in the Prophets;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical examples of prophets opposing kings or kings misusing power do not disprove the legal/rightful supremacy of the sovereign in religion; practice may vary from rightful claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three parts of Christ's office
rubrics_metrics.description: We find in Holy Scripture three parts of the Office of the Messiah: the first of a Redeemer, or Saviour: The second of a Pastor, Counsellour, or Teacher... The third of a King, and Eternall King, but under his Father...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hobbes treats Christ's roles as distinct functions with corresponding temporal dimensions: redemption (sacrifice), teaching/conversion (preaching and ministerial continuation), and eternal kingship (to be exercised after the Resurrection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Christ's kingdom not of this world; temporal obedience remains required
rubrics_metrics.description: My Kingdome is not of this world... the Kingdome of Christ is not to begin till the general Resurrection... our Saviour... 'I came not to judge the world, but to save the world.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Christ's earthly ministry does not displace present civil authority; his kingdom is future and eschatological, so Christians are commanded to obey existing magistrates and pay tribute to civil rulers while awaiting the heavenly reign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Christ's preaching did not contravene Jewish or Roman law
rubrics_metrics.description: The Preaching Of Christ Not Contrary To The Then Law Of The Jews, Nor Of Caesar... he taught all men to obey in the mean time them that sate in Moses chaire: he allowed them to give Caesar his tribute, and refused to take upon himselfe to be a Judg.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hobbes argues Christ's acts (preaching and miracles) were not legally seditious; Christ recognized and preserved the authority of contemporary institutions during his earthly ministry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Christ's kingship subordinate to the Father and analogous to Moses
rubrics_metrics.description: he is to be King then, no otherwise than as subordinate, or Viceregent of God the Father... the similitude with Moses... as Moses chose twelve Princes... so did our Saviour choose twelve Apostles, who shall sit on twelve thrones, and judge the twelve tribes of Israel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Christ's kingship, exercised in the world to come, is modelled on and subordinate to the Father; administrative structures (apostles, thrones) mirror Moses' institutions (twelve princes, seventy elders) as delegated authority within a divine polity.
